reading.body:
Flexential Fort Lauderdale publishes 3.15 MW of IT capacity across 64,164 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, that load supports roughly 315 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same 3.15 MW supports roughly 79 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is their claim. Either way, 3.15 MW is a small facility by the standards of purpose-built AI infrastructure, where individual training clusters routinely exceed it by an order of magnitude.

The certification stack qualifies this campus to host workloads under financial audit requirements (SOC 1 Type 2, SSAE 18), security and privacy audit requirements (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001), payment card data requirements (PCI DSS), and regulated health information requirements (HIPAA, HITRUST). That combination describes a compliance-oriented colocation environment. It says nothing about which tenants are present, and the operator has not published that information.

Within Florida, this site ranks first by published IT capacity among the three facilities this site has read with a MW figure, contributing 3.15 MW of the 7.54 MW total on record here, which is 42 percent of that narrow published pool. That figure reflects the limits of this site's data collection across 13 mapped Florida facilities, not a comprehensive view of Florida's data center market. For an organization weighing AI infrastructure in South Florida, this campus offers regulated compliance hosting at a scale that suits inference or enterprise workloads rather than large-scale model training.
